Form one decision per document from several reviewers

Source: R/doc-screen-reviewers.R
gr_reference_consensus.Rd

Turns a sheet that several people filled in into the reference gr_calibrate() compares the screener with: one consensus decision per document in human_decision, beside each reviewer's own.

Usage

gr_reference_consensus(
  reference,
  rule = c("majority", "any_include", "adjudicated")
)

Arguments

reference

The filled-in sheet: a data frame or a path to the CSV.

rule

How a disagreement is settled: "majority", "any_include" or "adjudicated".

Value

The sheet in wide form, one row per document, with human_decision holding the consensus and consensus_from how each row's was reached ("unanimous", "one reviewer", "majority", "tie kept", "any include", "adjudicated" or "no decision"). The rule is kept in the attribute consensus_rule, and the number of documents the reviewers disagreed on in conflicts.

Details

The sheet is the one gr_reference() writes with reviewers above 1, one human_decision_<reviewer> column per reviewer and a consensus column for an adjudicator. Reviewer columns can be renamed (human_decision_AB for a reviewer's initials, say): every human_decision_<x> column is read as one reviewer, except names ending in _note, _notes, _comment, _comments or _date, which are left alone, so give any other column of notes a name that does not start with human_decision_. A long sheet with one row per document per reviewer, a reviewer column and human_decision, is read too.

Where the reviewers who judged a record agree, that is its decision, under every rule; a record only one reviewer judged takes theirs. Where they disagree:

  • "majority": the decision of more than half of them. A tie is settled by the consensus column where it is filled, and otherwise as "include", so a reference never excludes a record half its reviewers included. With two reviewers every disagreement is a tie.

  • "any_include": "include" if any reviewer included it, the dual-screening convention of carrying a record forward unless both reviewers exclude it.

  • "adjudicated": the decision in consensus, which an adjudicator fills in; a disagreement with none is an error. A filled consensus takes precedence on every row, agreed or not.

gr_calibrate() given a multi-reviewer sheet without a consensus applies "adjudicated", so it stops on a disagreement nobody settled and says how many there were.

See also

gr_reference(), gr_calibrate()

Other corpus functions: gr_calibrate(), gr_inventory(), gr_records(), gr_reference(), gr_resolve(), gr_screen_sample_size(), gr_search()

Examples

sheet <- data.frame(document = paste0("d", 1:4, ".pdf"),
                    human_decision_1 = c("include", "include", "exclude", "exclude"),
                    human_decision_2 = c("include", "exclude", "exclude", "include"),
                    human_decision_3 = c("include", "exclude", "exclude", "exclude"),
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
gr_reference_consensus(sheet, "majority")[, c("document", "human_decision",
                                              "consensus_from")]
#>   document human_decision consensus_from
#> 1   d1.pdf        include      unanimous
#> 2   d2.pdf        exclude       majority
#> 3   d3.pdf        exclude      unanimous
#> 4   d4.pdf        exclude       majority
gr_reference_consensus(sheet, "any_include")$human_decision
#> [1] "include" "include" "exclude" "include"
